diagnosis: kernel_check_invariants aborted with 'unit large clause escaped propagation' (and, on sibling cases, the binary analog) — a clause left unit at a claimed propagation fixpoint. Root cause: backjump_apply_to, given a target ABOVE the pending learned clause's jump_level, asserted the UIP literal at the CURRENT decision level instead of its true assertion level. The random policy draws chronological backjump targets over [jump_level, current level] (backjump_instances enumerated them; the policy's dedicated Backjump branch also passes a random target). This kernel stamps every implication with the current decision level (kissat assign.c/backtrack.c), so the asserting literal was mis-leveled too deep; a subsequent partial Restart to a level between jump_level and that target unassigned it while its reason (learned) clause stayed unit at the retained lower levels — the unit then escaped propagation at the next fixpoint check. Same current-level-assignment hazard as corpus 004 (decide-on-unpropagated-trail), reached via chronological backtracking rather than deciding on an unpropagated trail; the large-clause and binary-clause escaped-unit signatures share this single cause. Never reachable in DefaultPolicy: its Backjump always targets jump_level (classic non-chronological CDCL) and it propagates to fixpoint before deciding, so every implication is stamped at its true level and no partial restart can strand one. Exposed only once V2 Backbone's high root-unit yield + the strengthened invariant checker (rev 30, which now flags escaped UNITS, not just escaped conflicts) made the mis-leveled-then-restart state common and eagerly caught under the random policy. Fixed 2026-07-16 (plan rev 31): backjump_apply_to clamps the target to jump_level (the only sound target under current-level assignment); backjump_instances offers only that canonical instance. The invariant restored: every literal is assigned at its TRUE level, so no backtrack can strand a still-implied literal's reason clause as an escaped unit. Genuine chronological backtracking (keeping decision levels above the assertion level) requires true-level assignment + chronological backtracking and remains the plan-§5.4 kernel candidate (first filed from corpus 002).
